summary: A sound stage-2 design. Warps own disjoint rows, the causal mask is right and the self-check is adequate, so it is worth one run as a rewrite. Its real risk is that A becomes ALU- or register-bound: four warps convert the same FP8 K/V tile four times, plus 4x mma.sync. Partials traffic is also 8x decode's, which stresses the <=130 us A+B target. Dispatch only after stage 1 (full-decode-cuda-splitkv-port) has run and its log shows the kernel compiled and self-checked, and on a check after the reset, not as a scored submit (risk high).
justification: Mechanism: at full verify_16/32 paired FA3 (153.3/296.3 us) streams the same page-1 KV gather as decode (146.8/289.0 us). FA3 verify costs only ~4% more than decode, so it is memory-bound, and LESSONS says this gather tops out at 1.3-1.7 TB/s. The attention port of the CUDA split-KV kernel A ran 111.4/245.5 us at decode_16/32 for the same bytes, so a verify kernel near that gather time would beat FA3 by ~30-45 us. The shape and load arithmetic checks out: verify_16 load is 46*462.4+16*603.9 = 30.9 ms, and 16*35 us = 0.56 ms is ~1.8%. verify_32: 16*45 of 44.3 ms is ~1.6%. The headline geomean moves ~0.5%, inside noise, so as the hypothesis says it must be judged on top_kernels per its Milestones. Decode rows (stage 1 kernel untouched), verify_1 (batch 1) and sliding rows are valid in-run controls. The causal bound t < cache_seqlens-7+i is correct (cache_seqlens = seq_lens+8, so token i sees keys <= seq_lens+i). Ragged lengths 1025/4097 already make chunks where tokens 0..6 are fully masked, which exercises the -inf partial path in the combine. Design soundness: the row-ownership layout (warp = kv head x 2 tokens x 8 heads, all 64 tokens of the tile) is the only one that keeps the accumulators in registers, and it uses all 16 mma rows (decode wasted 8). Weakest link 1, ALU: each tile's K and V are now converted e4m3->f16 by 4 warps per head instead of each warp converting a 16-token slice. That is 4x the cvt.rn.f16x2.e4m3x2 plus byte_perm work, about 4x2.5 MB of FP8 per SM at verify_16, on top of 4x the mma.sync (~41 GFLOP, ~70-100 us even at a good mma.sync rate). Compute that was hidden under the gather in decode may now be on the critical path. The stated fallback (an f16 smem tile per stage) costs ~32 KB per stage-slot and likely drops occupancy from 2 to 1 CTA/SM (stage 1 SMEM_A is ~93 KB, x2 = 186 of 228 KB). A better next-stage lever is QK^T with mma.sync m16n8k32 e4m3 (sm_89+/sm_90). Q and K are both already FP8, so it is exact, needs no K conversion and halves the QK mma count. Only V needs widening. Weakest link 2, registers: S 16x64 fp32 (32) + acc 16x64 (32) + Q A-frags for 4 k-steps (16) + P frags (16) + addressing is ~110-125 regs against the 128 cap of __launch_bounds__(256,2). Spills are likely. Weakest link 3, partials: 8 tokens x 16 heads x 64 fp32 = 32 KB per 1024-token item versus 4 KB in decode. That is ~40 MB written by A and re-read by the combine at verify_16 (~80 MB at verify_32), about 12% of the KV bytes, plausibly 10-20 us that the <=130 us A+B budget does not account for.
confounders: fa3-hdim128-head-pairing-batched: it defines the incumbent (paired FA3 + pad/unpad glue) that stage 2 replaces at verify_16/32. The saving is measured against the paired path, which is right, but it is conditional on pairing staying on master. If pairing were absent, the incumbent would be the unpaired FA3 (~7-13% slower on these shapes) and the gain would look larger. Not a confound that a companion needs to resolve.

paired-heads-pad-unpad-triton (in the judge now, not landed): it shrinks exactly the pad/unpad glue (~6.8 us x3) that this hypothesis counts in its verify_16/32 saving. If it lands before stage 2's base is cut, the expected saving drops by ~10-20 us per shape. Re-baseline the incumbent kernel sum from whichever master the branch is cut from, and merge carefully because both edit the same paired branch of kernel_fn.

marlin-block-m-cap-16: no mechanistic interaction (it is MoE, not attention). Marlin is still 48-51% of full verify_16/32 (284/501 us), and its run-to-run drift can mask a 30-45 us attention change in the per-shape row, so read the replaced kernels' own us in top_kernels.

post-expert-norm-triton-small-t, sglang-pipeline-parity-router-hilo-m8: no interaction with the target shapes. The post-norm path is gated to small T and does not run at T=128/256. The router is unrelated.
interference: No companion is warranted. This is a rewrite stage judged on the replaced kernels' own time against the incumbent and the floor. The decisive evidence is in the profile: splitkv_attn_verify_kernel + splitkv_combine_verify_kernel us at full verify_16/32, compared with paired FA3 main + combine + pad/unpad + FusedRMSNormGate from master. The run carries its own controls: decode rows run the unchanged stage 1 kernel, and verify_1, decode_1 and every sliding row run master code. An ab-revert of pairing would only re-measure FA3 unpaired, which is already known. The useful follow-ups (e4m3 mma for QK, a larger verify chunk to cut partials traffic, launch_bounds adjustments) belong in stage 3, not here. Sequencing note: stage 1 has not run on muse_decode_layer yet. Building on unharvested stage-1 code risks spending a check on a fallback run, so dispatch only after stage 1 harvests with '[splitkv] load_inline compiled' and no 'SELF-CHECK FAILED' in its log.
rules_flags: None blocking. FP8 E4M3 queries are allowed. FP8->f16 widening is exact. P in f16 with fp32 accumulation is finer than FA3's own. Workspace and grid come from shapes and device properties only. The prepare() self-check uses synthetic tensors, not data. There are no host syncs.

Every key / correctness wording: 'masked tokens never dereferenced, zero-filled' must apply only to t >= cache_seqlens[b]. Keys that are causally masked for early query tokens but visible to later ones must still be loaded, and masked per row in the score (rows quad and quad+8 are different tokens with different bounds). Mask in registers only, never by skipping loads of in-range tokens, and never skip tiles by attention weight.

Harvest guard (DECISIONS 2026-10-24T141733Z): if load_inline fails or the self-check fails, the run silently measures master. Read the log tail before judging, and make the q_len 8 self-check failure disable only the verify gate (or the whole _EXT), with a printed reason.
open_questions: What are the register count and spills of splitkv_attn_verify_kernel under __launch_bounds__(256,2)? Add -Xptxas -v (or print the cudaFuncGetAttributes numRegs/localSizeBytes) to the log so the harvest can tell ALU-bound from spill-bound.

How does combine time scale with 8x larger partials (~40/80 MB at verify_16/32)? Would a 2048-token verify chunk (halving partials, still ~600 items vs 264 CTAs) be the cheaper stage-3 lever compared with conversion work?
If A exceeds ~150 us at verify_16, is QK^T via mma.sync m16n8k32 e4m3 (no K conversion, exact) preferable to the f16 smem tile, which likely costs the second CTA per SM?
Which incumbent glue is on the base master: does paired-heads-pad-unpad-triton land first? The expected verify savings should be restated against that base.

Is the verify_16/32 'agentic' spread's max page_table width large enough that the workspace (B*max_chunks*8*16*64*4 bytes) inside graph capture is a concern? At verify_32 it is roughly 32*max_chunks*32 KB.
